item.title: Trump wants Greenland, Mette Frederiksen warns: "He should be taken seriously"
item.description: Denmark's prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, has warned that Donald Trump's repeated remarks about taking control of Greenland should not be dismissed as rhetoric, saying she believes the United States president is serious about his intentions toward the Arctic territory. You might be interested: Trump rekindles concerns in Denmark: "We do need Greenland". Speaking on Monday to Danish public broadcaster DR, Frederiksen said both Denmark and Greenland have made their positions unmistakably clear.

item.title: Olympique Lyonnais explains details about Endrick deal, who wants to "win titles" for Lyon
item.description: Endrick has officially been introduced today as new Olympique Lyon player, but only for six months. item.title: Starmer backs Mette Frederiksen after Trump renews threats over Greenland: "I stand with her"
item.description: The UK has thrown its support behind Denmark after Trump once again suggested that Greenland should come under American control, prompting renewed concern among European allies. Speaking on Monday, Prime Minister Keir Starmer said the future of the mineral-rich Arctic territory rests solely with Greenland and the Kingdom of Denmark. item.title: Bluefin tuna fetches record $3.2 million at Tokyo's New Year auction: "Hoping it would be a bit cheaper"
item.description: Like every year, Japan welcomes the New Year with its most famous fish auction. This time, however, the numbers were unlike anything seen before: $3.2 million, to be exact. A massive Pacific bluefin tuna sold for a staggering $3.2 million at Tokyo's famed Toyosu fish market on Monday, setting a new record.
